newsitem.title: USA: Muni credit spreads tighten in past week -- Delphis.
newsitem.headline: Muni credit spreads tighten in past week -- Delphis.

text.p: Credit spreads among high-grade municipal bonds tightened five to 10 basis points in the week ended Thursday, adding to similar moves the prior week, Delphis Hanover Corp. said Friday.
The credit spread between Aaa-rated and Baa-rated one-year bonds tightened five basis points, to 65 basis points, after tightening 10 the week before.
The 30-year credit spread tightened 10 for the second consecutive week, leaving 60 basis points to separate average yields on Aaa-rated and Baa-rated 30-year munis.
The municipal yield curve held mostly steady for the week, after flattening an average of 10 basis points the week before.
The spread between one-year and 30-year bonds in the triple-A category was unchanged at 175 basis points. The Baa yield curve flattened five basis points, to 170.
Average yields on one-year, Aaa-rated municipal bonds rose five basis points to 3.65 percent. Baa-rated one-year bonds were unchanged at 4.30 percent, after falling 15 the week before.

In the intermediate sector, yields on Aaa-rated 10-year bonds fell five basis points to 4.70 percent, after dropping 10 the prior week. Baa-rated ten-years fell 10 to 5.35 percent, after falling 20 the prior week.
Munis underperformed the Treasury market over the week.

The yield on the government long bond fell 10 basis points for the third consecutive week, moving to 6.68 percent. Thirty-year Aaa-rated municipal yields, meanwhile, rose five basis points over the same period to 5.40 percent, after dropping 15 basis points the previous week.
Yields were down five basis points on 30-year, Baa-rated bonds, moving to six percent, after dropping 25 the week before.
Thirty-year, Aaa-rated munis yielded 80.8 percent of the Treasury long bond at the close Thursday, compared to 78.9 percent the week before.
